jobs.description:
HR Manager

Take responsibility for HR operations, employee development and people management in an international project organisation.

Copenhagen Group A/S is a Danish project-driven company with a strong international profile.

We tender for and manage complex projects for international organisations and national authorities and, as the parent company of several specialised subsidiaries, provide the shared structure that ensures consistency across the Group.

Our activities span different markets, projects and stakeholders, placing high demands on structured HR processes and effective people management.

To support this, we are looking for an experienced and proactive HR Manager to take overall responsibility for HR activities and contribute to the continued development of the organisation.

Your Responsibilities

You will be responsible for managing and developing HR activities across Copenhagen Group, ensuring consistent and effective processes that support employees and management.

Your responsibilities will include personnel administration and the development and maintenance of HR policies, procedures and systems.

You will work closely with management on employee relations, organisational development, employee engagement, training and professional development

You will also ensure compliance with relevant employment legislation, maintain accurate employee records and provide management with HR data and guidance to support informed decision-making.

The role requires you to work independently, take ownership of HR processes and initiatives, and promote a positive working environment across the Group.

Your Background

We are looking for someone with proven experience in HR management or a similar role, including responsibility for HR processes, employee relations and personnel administration.

You have solid knowledge of Danish employment legislation and HR best practices, along with practical experience in recruitment, HR systems and employee development.

You are structured, reliable and proactive, with strong organisational skills, attention to detail and the ability to balance strategic initiatives with day-to-day responsibilities.

You have excellent interpersonal skills, exercise sound judgement and handle confidential matters with professionalism and discretion.

You communicate fluently in Danish and English, both verbally and in writing.

A relevant educational background in HR, business administration or a related field is required.

Practical Information

The position is based at our office in Copenhagen.

We offer a key position with a high degree of independence and responsibility, where you will have significant influence on HR practices and organisational development across Copenhagen Group.

Salary will reflect qualifications and experience.

Employment is conditional upon obtaining the required security clearance.

Do you want to join a global leader in renewable energy infrastructure? If so, CIP Fund Solutions (CIP FS) is looking for an Analyst to join our office in Copenhagen, Denmark.

Team

You will join a dynamic and collaborative finance team working across multiple international entities. The team consists of Financial Controllers based in London, Sheffield, Madrid, and Copenhagen, creating a diverse and international working environment. The role is based in our Copenhagen office, and you will work closely with and report to the Copenhagen based team.

We are responsible for financial reporting, accounting, and compliance for a broad portfolio of companies, and we collaborate closely with both internal stakeholders and external advisors across EMEA region. The team values accuracy, ownership, and clear communication, while maintaining a supportive and informal culture where collaboration and continuous learning are key.

Role

You will become an integral part of our expanding team in Accounting, Compliance, and Controlling team for EMEA. We are committed to supporting your professional development and providing valuable learning opportunities.

The role offers broad exposure to finance, accounting, compliance, and corporate administration across a portfolio of international renewable energy investments. You will support the Financial Controllers with recurring accounting and controlling activities, while also assisting with KYC processes, banking documentation, and other corporate and regulatory requirements applicable to our entities.

You will work closely with internal stakeholders, banks, auditors, legal advisers, corporate service providers, and other external counterparties. Through this combination of responsibilities, you will gain practical experience in how international investment structures are established, financed, administered, and maintained throughout their lifecycle.

Responsibilities will consist of but are not limited to:

• Supporting recurring accounting and controlling activities, including cost controlling, balance-sheet controlling, reconciliations, and monitoring of equity contributions

• Reviewing and processing financial information, internal reports, annual reports, and tax-related documentation

• Assisting with KYC and due-diligence requests from banks, auditors, etc.

• Supporting the opening, maintenance, and closure of bank accounts, including the preparation and coordination of required forms, supporting documentation, signatures, and internal approvals

• Assisting with bank-access administration and the maintenance of authorized users and signatories

You

You are a final-year BSc or first-year MSc student in Finance, Economics, Business, Accounting, Auditing, Business Law, or another relevant field. You are motivated by transforming theory into practical solutions and are interested in gaining broad experience across finance, accounting, banking, compliance, and corporate administration.

You enjoy working with both numbers and documentation and are comfortable coordinating tasks involving several stakeholders. You work in an organized way, pay close attention to detail, and see tasks through to completion.

We look for the following in a candidate:

• Structured problem-solving skills and a responsible approach to tasks

• Close attention to detail and a high level of accuracy

• An interest in operational finance, accounting, compliance

• Ability to follow up effectively with internal and external stakeholders

• Proficiency in English, both in writing and speaking, paired with effective communication skills

• Previous experience within finance, accounting, banking, compliance, legal administration, or a similar area is beneficial but not a requirement.

The process

Please apply online as soon as possible as applications will be processed on an ongoing basis. For questions related to the role, please reach out to our Talent Acquisition team at recruitment@cipfs.com. We do not include CV's and Cover Letters sent by email.

As we continue to improve our candidate experience, diversity and avoid unconscious bias, please avoid having a photo in your CV. We commit to an inclusive recruitment process and equality for all applicants.

Please be aware that we will not accept speculative CV submissions for any of our roles from recruitment agencies, and any unsolicited candidate submissions will be exempt from any payment expectations and ownership.

---

CIP Fund Solutions’ commitment to diversity and inclusion

CIP Fund Solutions is committed to securing a diverse and inclusive work environment where everyone feels respected and heard.

A diverse workforce allows CIP Fund Solutions to achieve results through different approaches and solutions to task execution and problem solving. We want all our employees to have equal opportunities for personal growth and career opportunities regardless of age, gender, sexual orientation, disability, religion, nationality, or ethnicity.

CIP Fund Solutions

CIP FS’ purpose is to enable CIP’s ambition to scale rapidly over the coming strategy-period - supporting our colleagues with professional and efficient financial, legal, tax and business operations through the cycle from fund formation and capital raising, to deploying investments into construction of large-scale greenfield renewable energy assets, as well as M&A.

For more information, please visit CIP Fund Solutions.

Are you ready to combine hands-on IT support with technical development in an international shipping company?

At Clipper Bulk, we are looking for an IT Operations & Support Specialist to join our IT team at our headquarters in Copenhagen.

This is an opportunity to become a key part of our IT function, ensuring reliable day-to-day support while gradually taking on broader responsibilities within IT operations, Microsoft 365 and infrastructure.

As IT Operations & Support Specialist, you will play an important role in keeping our IT environment running smoothly and supporting colleagues across the organisation. You will take ownership of daily IT support in close collaboration with the rest of the IT team, while also contributing to the maintenance, improvement and development of our IT systems.

Over time, you will have the opportunity to take on greater responsibility for operational tasks and smaller IT projects.

What will be your responsibilities:

Your responsibilities will include, but are not limited to:

• Providing hands-on IT support and troubleshooting for colleagues

• Managing and maintaining Microsoft 365 services, including Entra ID, Exchange Online and Intune

• Supporting device management, user administration and employee onboarding and offboarding

• Handling day-to-day IT operational tasks and ensuring system stability

• Supporting identity and access management, endpoint security and IT infrastructure

• Maintaining IT documentation, procedures and best practices

• Identifying opportunities to improve and automate IT processes

• Participating in smaller IT operations and infrastructure projects

• Collaborating with internal stakeholders and external IT service providers

What we are looking for:

At Clipper, our employees shape our work environment, so bringing a positive attitude is essential.

We are looking for someone who genuinely enjoys both IT support and technical operations. You are comfortable taking responsibility for day-to-day support, but you are also curious about the technology behind the systems and motivated to expand your technical capabilities. You don't just wait for the next support ticket. You take initiative, identify opportunities for improvement and follow tasks through to completion.

We imagine that you bring:

• Practical experience with IT support and technical troubleshooting

• Experience with Microsoft 365 administration, including Entra ID and related services

• Knowledge of Microsoft Intune, endpoint management and Windows client administration

• A good understanding of user management, access rights and IT security principles

• A structured and independent approach to solving technical challenges

• Good communication skills and a service-minded attitude

• Strong English communication skills, both written and spoken

• Experience with IT security and endpoint security solutions, network infrastructure, PowerShell, IT automation, identity and access management, IT projects or AI tools such as Microsoft Copilot would be an advantage, but is not a requirement

• Minimum 5 years of relevant experience

If you’re enthusiastic about this role but your experience doesn’t align perfectly with each qualification, we still encourage you to apply. You could be the ideal candidate for this position, or for another opportunity with us.

What you will love about us

At Clipper, you will become part of a growing and professional work environment where we strive to be the best. We offer:

• A varied role combining hands-on support, IT operations and technical development.

• The opportunity to gradually expand your responsibilities and technical expertise.

• Close collaboration with experienced IT colleagues.

• An international working environment with colleagues across our global offices.

• A welcoming and inclusive work environment with a variety of socal, sports, and cultural events throughout the year

• Attractive employee benefits, including pension, health, dental and critical ilness insurance

• Beautiful office facilities in Nordhavn, located near the metro with on-site parking, delicious lunch arangement and access to fitness facilities and a personal trainer.

Application and recruitment process:

Please submit your CV and cover letter through our application portal by 29th November 2026.

Applications will be reviewed on an ongoing basis and interviews will be treated with full discretion.

The recruitment process consists of two interview rounds. Shortlisted candidates will be invited to a first interview conducted via video call. Candidates progressing to the second round will be invited to an in-person interview and asked to complete a personality assessment and a logical reasoning test beforehand. Confidential reference checks will be conducted for final candidates.

Learn more about Clipper at clipper-bulk.com, LinkedIn, and Instagram.

Clipper is an industry leader in dry bulk, an operator, a pool manager, and a specialist in steel services. We operate a modern fleet of approximately 120 handysize and supramax vessels, transporting a wide range of cargo from dry bulk to break bulk. Clipper is commercially headquartered in Copenhagen and employs a staff of around 100 onshore worldwide__. We are a global workplace built on five shared values: Dependable, Curious, Collaboration, Hands-on and Family. We believe in learning from one another and welcome people with a growth mindset and ambition.

Sustainability initiatives - we strive to make a positive impact. As a maritime player with a global presence at sea and onshore, we recognize our social, environmental, and ethical responsibility. We push for positive development by responsibly running our business and promoting sustainable business behavior in our network. Read more about sustainability initiatives on our website.

At Acodyne, you will help develop the software, high-power electronics, and robotic systems that bring our next generation of high-speed, heavy-lift cargo UAS to life, moving between code, schematics, the lab bench, and real flight hardware.

Your Role

You Will Work Closely With Our CTO And Engineering Team On The Electrical And Software Systems That Power And Control Our Aircraft. From Firmware To High-power Distribution, This Is As Real As Engineering Gets. You Will

• 
Develop and test embedded software and firmware for flight-critical and ground systems (C/C++, Python)

• 
Design, build, and test high-power electronics such as power distribution, battery systems, and motor drives

• 
Integrate sensors, actuators, and robotic/autonomous subsystems into the aircraft and ground equipment

• 
Develop tools for test automation, data logging, and analysis

• 
Bring up, debug, and validate hardware on the bench and during flight tests

• 
Document designs, code, and test results for certification purposes

**About You

**You enjoy writing code as much as holding an oscilloscope probe or a soldering iron. You're the type who builds things outside class and wants to take that to the next level. You likely:

• 
Are currently pursuing a degree in electrical engineering, software/computer engineering, robotics, mechatronics, or similar

• 
Have programming experience in C/C++ and/or Python

• 
Have a solid understanding of electronics and circuit design

• 
Enjoy hands-on lab work, prototyping, and debugging real hardware

• 
Are curious about UAVs, robotics, or high-performance systems

• 
Are proactive, independent, and eager to learn fast

**Nice To Have

**

• 
Experience with power electronics, high-voltage systems, motor control, or battery management systems (BMS)

• 
Experience with embedded platforms (STM32, ARM, etc.), RTOS, or communication buses (CAN, UART, SPI, I²C)

• 
Exposure to ROS, PX4/ArduPilot, or control and autonomy algorithms

• 
PCB design experience (KiCad, Altium, etc.)

**About Acodyne

**We are a UAS company developing heavy-lift, high-speed eVTOL UAS for defence and industrial logistics. We are currently 18 people, based at our workshop at Avedøre Airfield, and plan to double our team in the next year.

**About The Internship

**

• 
Duration: Full-time for 5–6 months, with start in January/February 2027.

• 
Time off: 2.08 vacation days per month + Danish public holidays.

• 
Location: Avedøre Flyveplads, workshop-based, approximately 45 minutes by public transport from Copenhagen city center.

• 
Compensation: DKK 6,000-8,000 per month before tax. Please note this is a contribution to living and transport. It will likely not cover full living costs. Interns are expected to supplement with grants or other funding.

• 
Visa: Acodyne is unfortunately not able to help obtain a work visa. It is expected that the candidate has a legal right to work in Denmark.

• 
Please note: The internship opportunity is intended for currently enrolled students who wish to gain relevant work experience as part of their studies. We particularly encourage applications from students who are able to use the internship as an integrated part of their degree programme, for example through ECTS credits, a project-based internship, or another formal study-related arrangement.

jobs.occupation: Women’s Academy 2027: Insights into the financial sector
jobs.description:
Step inside the world of finance and explore what happens on a busy trading floor, how major companies are financed and how a bank manages risk in changing markets and society. Women’s Academy is an 8-week student programme at Danske Bank’s headquarters, designed to give you first-hand insight into Large Corporates & Institutions and Group Risk & Compliance.

What you will be doing

Across eight weekly sessions, you will meet specialists from across Danske Bank who will introduce you to their work, share real perspectives from the industry and involve you in relevant business topics.

During the programme, you will:

• 
Explore areas such as Corporate Banking, Markets, Corporate Finance, Risk and Compliance

• 
Gain insight into how different parts of Danske Bank work together

• 
Work with practical topics linked to finance, risk and business decisions

• 
Hear directly from people working in the financial sector

• 
Meet other students who are curious about finance

• 
Become part of the Women’s Academy community

• 
Take part in a celebratory dinner at the end of the programme

• 
Receive a certificate of participation upon completing the Academy

The Academy was created to encourage more women to explore finance. Women are still underrepresented in several parts of the sector, and by opening our doors, sharing knowledge and providing access to role models, we want to make finance feel more accessible to a broader range of students.

About you

We welcome applications from university students between the second year of their bachelor’s degree and the second year of their master’s degree.

You do not need previous experience in banking or finance. You also do not need to know whether finance is the right career path for you yet. The Academy is a place to explore the sector from within and discover what captures your interest.

We are looking for students who:

• 
Are curious about finance, business, markets or risk

• 
Want to learn more about career opportunities in the financial sector

• 
Are motivated to take an active part in discussions and sessions

• 
Bring an open mindset and a willingness to explore new topics

• 
Come from any academic background and are interested in learning from others

Practical information

• 
Programme period: 8 weeks in Q1 2027

• 
Duration: Eight weekly sessions of approximately three hours

• 
Location: Danske Bank headquarters, Copenhagen

• 
Application window: 2 November-23 November

• 
Attendance: Participants are expected to attend all eight sessions

What we offer you

You will get a unique opportunity to experience the financial sector from the inside, meet specialists from across Danske Bank and build your understanding of how finance connects to companies, markets and society. You will also become part of a student community and gain access to people who can share their experiences, career paths and advice.

Are you ready to explore finance?

To apply, please submit your CV and answer five short questions about your motivation, what makes you curious about finance and what you hope to gain from Women’s Academy. Instead of submitting a cover letter, we would like to get to know your perspective through your answers. There are no right or wrong answers, and previous experience in banking or finance is not required. We encourage you to respond openly and honestly, drawing on the experiences that are meaningful to you, whether they come from your studies, work, interests or personal life.

• 
Tell us briefly about yourself and what currently interests you.

Maximum 100 words

• 
What motivated you to apply for Women’s Academy, and what makes you curious about the financial sector?

Maximum 150 words

• 
Tell us about something you have achieved that you are proud of. Why is it meaningful to you?

This can come from your studies, work, volunteering, hobbies or personal life. Maximum 150 words.

• 
What motivates or drives you when learning something new?

Maximum 100 words

• 
What do you hope to gain from Women’s Academy, and how would you contribute to the programme?

Maximum 150 words

For further information please contact:

• 
Victoria Witzeling, DEI Lead LC&I and BC, at viwi@danskebank.dk or +45 20 65 21 34

• 
Magnus Ulstrup, DEI Lead & Senior Transformation Consultant, Group Risk & Compliance, at magnus@danskebank.dk or +45 30 11 83 65

• 
Filippa Kjær, DEI Lead Student, at fkja@danskebank.dk

Join Danske Bank’s Women’s Academy and take your first step into the world of finance. We look forward to hearing from you!

jobs.occupation: Analyst in Capital Planning – Help Shape the Bank’s Financial Future
jobs.description:
Capital planning sits at the heart of how Danske Bank balances financial resilience with sustainable growth. As part of a close-knit analytical team, you will contribute to decisions that enable the bank to serve its customers and support its strategic ambitions. This is a role where your work genuinely matters and where you will build a solid foundation in capital management.

What you will be doing

The Capital Planning team is part of Financial Resource Management in Group Treasury, sitting within Danske Bank's CFO area. The team of seven works on capital target setting, capital issuances, dividend decisions and macroeconomic stress testing. Your analyses and reports will receive close attention from the Executive Leadership Team, the Board of Directors and financial regulators. The atmosphere is collaborative, with knowledge sharing and learning woven into everyday working life, and the team takes pride in delivering high-quality work while enjoying the process.

More specifically, you will:

• Support monthly capital and MREL assessments and projections

• Analyse the effects of regulatory and model changes with relevant teams

• Contribute to stress tests and assessments of capital targets and buffers

• Help analyse payout capacity and capital and MREL funding needs

• Prepare decision material and gradually take ownership of defined deliverables

About you

• Master's degree in economics, finance, business administration or a related field

• Strong analytical skills and a structured, detail-oriented approach

• Ability to communicate complex findings clearly in English

• Curious and collaborative, with an interest in learning and developing within the field

• Comfortable working independently on defined tasks while contributing to team goals

Experience in banking or capital management, and familiarity with Python, SQL or similar tools, would be a welcome addition. We consider candidates at different stages of their career, so we encourage you to apply whether you are just starting out or bring a few years of relevant experience.

What we offer you

You will join a dedicated team where collaboration and continuous learning are part of daily work. We work in a hybrid model, with three to four days per week in the office to support knowledge sharing and team cohesion. You will have room to develop your analytical skills, deepen your understanding of capital management, and take on increasing responsibility over time.

Are you ready for the next step?

If this sounds like the right opportunity for you, we would be glad to hear from you. Feel free to reach out to hiring manager Henrik Bang at hban@danskebank.dk if you have any questions about the role before applying.

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible or by 22 November 2026 at the latest.

We look forward to hearing from you!

Danske Bank

København V, 1600 København V Besøg hjemmeside

Kontaktperson

Henrik Bang hban@danskebank.dk

Ansøgningsfrist

22. november 2026

About the Team

At the Enterprise Process Management (EPM) unit, our north star is “Partnering towards process excellence.” As Danske Bank’s internal consultancy, the Process Intelligence team collaborates across the organization to drive impactful process improvements and embed operational excellence, deliivering real value. We work side-by-side with business units and agile tribes, supporting strategic growth initiatives and fostering a culture of continuous improvement.

Our Process Partners play a key role in driving transformations for efficiency and building capabilities in process management. By leveraging Lean methodologies and best practices, we help optimize processes, reduce waste, enhance customer satisfaction and regulatory compliance, and strengthen the organization’s ability to deliver sustainable results. We coach leaders to translate operational excellence principles into lasting behavioural change

What You Will Do

• Drive end-to-end process optimization initiatives, applying Lean principles and eliminating waste.

• Lead and participate in projects focused on customer journeys, process transformation, and change management, using methods such as DMAIC.

• Identify and prioritize organizational benefits, aligning process improvements with business goals and customer needs.

• Acquire and analyze data to uncover improvement opportunities, utilizing Lean and Six Sigma tools and statistical concepts.

• Develop and operationalize process improvement frameworks, ensuring the sustainability and control of implemented solutions.

• Deliver training and mentor colleagues on Lean and process improvement methods, fostering leadership development (both self and others) and a culture of continuous improvement.

• Champion operational excellence by designing and implementing best practices that enhance process performance, ensure compliance, and support the organization’s strategic objectives.

• Coach leaders to embed operational excellence into daily management practices, driving sustainable behavioral change and a culture of continuous improvement.

What We’re Looking For

• Green/Black Belt certification in Lean & Six Sigma, certified Lean Manager or equivalent

• 3+ years of experience in process re-engineering, operational excellence, optimization, or transformation, with strong data analysis skills.

• Project/program management experience (e.g., Agile, Prince2, PMP), with process management or operational excellence as a core methodology.

• Strong skills in business process improvement, change management, and stakeholder engagement.

• Ability to influence without formal authority and thrive in a large, complex organization.

• Experience in delivering training or mentoring on Lean/process improvement.

• Systemic thinking, pragmatic problem-solving, and the ability to structure ambiguity.

• Proven track record in driving and anchoring sustainable change.

• Demonstrated experience in operational excellence, coaching leaders with a proven ability to drive sustainable improvements in efficiency, quality, and business outcomes.

• As an advantage: knowledge in AI application for process and operational excellence work.

• Advanced English language skills

Want to Know More?

If you have any questions, you are welcome to reach out to Laura Makele, Head of Process Intelligence on lmak@danskebank.lt or Indre Sliziene, Head of Operational Excellence on isli@danskebank.lt

Diversity & Inclusion

Together, we continue to build an inclusive culture that encourages, supports, and celebrates diversity.

jobs.occupation: Finance Business Partner – Large Corporates & Institutions
jobs.description:
Danske Bank is the preferred bank for large corporate and institutional customers across the Nordics, and this role sits at the heart of the financial steering that helps LC&I deliver on that promise. As Finance Business Partner for the Markets IT Development area, you will translate financial insight into decisions that shape how three Tribes operate and invest. In return, you will grow your career within a collaborative team that values openness and genuine flexibility.

What you will be doing

You will join a dedicated team of Finance Business Partners anchored in LC&I Performance Management within the CFO Area. The team works closely with senior management across Markets IT Development, Payments, and Asset Management, sharing analysis that feeds directly into financial steering decisions. The atmosphere is informal and collaborative, with a shared belief that clear financial insight creates real value for the business.

In your day-to-day work, you will:

• Act as Finance Business Partner for the Markets IT Development area, covering three Tribes

• Represent the CFO Area in the area's management team meetings

• Coordinate monthly and annual financial planning and analysis processes

• Assess financial implications of prioritisation decisions and track expected benefits

• Support a more data-driven approach to decision-making across the area

About you

• Relevant master's-level degree in finance, economics, or a related field

• Experience in FP&A, performance management, or business partnering is beneficial but not required

• Ability to build trusted relationships with senior stakeholders through clear communication

• Interest in data analytics and digitisation; strong Excel skills are an advantage

• Comfortable navigating a large, complex organisation with multiple priorities

• Proficient in written and spoken English

If you have experience working alongside IT development teams or within a financial institution, that would be a welcome addition to the team.

What we offer you

This role offers you the chance to develop your finance career within one of the leading Nordic banks, working alongside colleagues who are genuinely committed to collaboration and knowledge sharing. We work in a hybrid model with three to four days per week in the office, balancing flexibility with a strong team culture. You will have access to learning opportunities and a working environment that encourages new approaches and personal growth.

Are you ready for the next step?

If this sounds like the right opportunity for you, we encourage you to apply. Feel free to reach out to hiring manager, Muhammad Zohaib, at zoh@danskebank.dk or Strategic Investment Partner, Daniel Bahne Kvesel, at dakv@danskebank.dk if you have any questions about the role before applying.

We review applications on an ongoing basis, so we encourage you to apply as soon as possible or by 22 November 2026 at the latest.

We look forward to hearing from you!

Operational information is the backbone of how a bank operates, and getting it right matters.

We are looking for an experienced and strategic leader to strengthen the Group-wide operational information blueprint, with accountability anchored in the Operational Design & Governance team within Enterprise Process Management.

In this role, you will lead a critical Group-wide capability, strengthening how we design, structure and govern operational information across the Group. You will strengthen the foundations for simpler and more transparent operations, effective transformation, regulatory readiness, automation and AI adoption.

Your role

Your mission is to mature and strengthen the Group-wide operational information model, making it increasingly coherent, consistent, scalable and fit for both commercial and regulatory needs, while driving its adoption across the organisation.

You will lead a team of 16 specialists within Enterprise Process Management and own the direction and evolution of the Group’s operational information capability. Working across organisational boundaries, you will collaborate closely with Business Units, Enterprise Architecture, Risk, Compliance, Technology and Transformation teams.

More specifically, you will:

• 
Lead and develop a high-performing team of specialists while building a collaborative and outcome-focused culture.

• 
Set clear direction for the Group operational information model design and establish clear methodologies, standards and governance across the Group.

• 
Strengthen operational governance and accountability across functions, value chains, business services, processes, manual services, SOPs and business procedures.

• 
Drive adoption and execution, ensuring frameworks and standards translate into practical and scalable solutions across the Bank.

• 
Create foundations for AI, automation and data-driven operations through high-quality operational information and strong design principles.

• 
Partner across the Bank, connecting business, operations, architecture, technology, data, risk, controls and transformation perspectives.

• 
Advise and guide senior stakeholders on operational information design, governance and operating model decisions.

What we are looking for

You are an experienced and strategic leader who combines enterprise thinking with the ability to turn direction into execution.

You bring:

•

The Human-Centred Computing Section, Department of Computer Science, invites applicants for a PhD fellowship in Human-Computer Interaction.

  Start date is (expected to be) 1 March or as soon as possible thereafter.

  The project
 Digital technologies increasingly mediate how people experience, understand and respond to their bodies. The PhD project will investigate the relationship between bodies, technology and chronic illness, with a particular focus on self-tracking technologies. The project will explore how people with chronic conditions engage with these technologies and how technologies shape interactions with informal caregivers and health professionals. The project will critically examine how these technologies enact particular understandings of bodily difference and chronic illness, and how such understandings intersect with broader social, cultural and political norms. Within this topic, the PhD student will have some freedom to shape the focus of their work and the research questions they are interested in.

  The project will employ qualitative, participatory and design-oriented methods, with a particular emphasis on co-design and Research through Design. Co-design will involve working collaboratively with people with chronic conditions and other relevant stakeholders to explore their experiences of their bodies and technologies, and to imagine and develop new forms of technological interaction. Through Research through Design, the PhD researcher will develop and study experimental technological prototypes as a way of investigating alternative ways of sensing, representing and interacting with bodies. Design will be used not only to develop technological artefacts, but also as a means of generating knowledge about societal norms around chronic illness and the relationship between people and technology.

  Who are we looking for?
 We are looking for candidates within the field(s) of human-computer interaction (HCI). The ideal candidate should have a strong background in user-centred research methods, with some experience of working in a research environment. We are particularly interested in candidates who have experience in conducting design processes and developing both screen-based and physical computing prototypes. It is expected that candidates will have an M.Sc. degree in a relevant technical, design, or social science discipline. In addition, the ideal candidate will be able to document research capabilities (e.g., a thesis, publication, or project portfolio), have strong recommendations from supervisors and mentors, and possess a high level of intellectual humility. Preferred candidates would have advanced Danish language proficiency.

  Our group and research- and what do we offer?
 The PhD fellow will become a member of the Human-Centered Computing (HCC) research section at the University of Copenhagen’s Department of Computer Science. Here, we aim to fundamentally understand and improve the relation between computational technology and people. We are currently the top-ranked HCI research group in Europe (https://csrankings.org/#/index?chi&europe). Our research focuses on using computing to support people’s activities and well-being; inventing new ways for people to interact with technology, and understanding how human capabilities are influenced by technology. At the HCC section, we are currently over 15 faculty members, and over 20 postdoctoral researchers, PhD students, and research assistants. We hold joint weekly research meetings, many annual retreats, and have a thriving social environment from daily lunches to larger events. We attend the most important international conferences, such as CHI. We particularly value having a supportive and collegial work environment that values and encourages diversity. 

  Copenhagen is a vibrant city, with many cultural offerings and easy access to the rest of Europe. For more information about working in Denmark, consult International Staff Mobility.

  Principal supervisor is Associate Professor Tariq Andersen, Department of Computer Science, tariq@di.ku.dk. The PhD project is led by Assistant Professor Sarah Homewood, Department of Computer Science, sfh@di.ku.dk, 31606109.

  The PhD programme 
 Depending of your level of education, you can undertake the PhD programme as either:

  Option A: A three year full-time study within the framework of the regular PhD programme (5+3 scheme), if you already have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master’s degree.

  Option B: An up to five year full-time study programme within the framework of the integrated MSc and PhD programme (the 3+5 scheme), if you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree – but you have an education equivalent to a Danish bachelors´s degree.

   Option A: Getting into a position on the regular PhD programme 

  Qualifications needed for the regular programme
 To be eligible for the regular PhD programme, you must have completed a degree programme, equivalent to a Danish master’s degree (180 ECTS/3 FTE BSc + 120 ECTS/2 FTE MSc) related to the subject area of the project, e.g. Computer Science. For information of eligibility of completed programmes, see General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.

  Terms of employment in the regular programme 

  Employment as PhD fellow is full time and for maximum 3 years.

  Employment is conditional upon your successful enrolment as a PhD student at the PhD School at the Faculy of Science, University of Copenhagen. This requires submission and acceptance of an application for the specific project formulated by the applicant.

  Terms of appointment and payment accord to the agreement between the Danish Ministry of Taxation and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State. The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

   Option B: Getting into a position on the integrated MSc and PhD programme

  Qualifications needed for the integrated MSc and PhD programme 

  If you do not have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish master´s degree, you might be qualified for the integrated MSc and PhD programme, if you have an education equivalent to a relevant Danish bachelor´s degree. Here you can find out, if that is relevant for you: General assessments for specific countries and Assessment database.  

  Terms of the integrated programme
 To be eligible for the integrated scholarship, you are (or are eligible to be) enrolled at one of the faculty’s master programmes in Computer Science.

  Students on the integrated programme will enroll as PhD students simultaneously with completing their enrollment in this MSc degree programme.

  The duration of the integrated programme is up to five years, and depends on the amount of credits that you have passed on your MSc programme. For further information about the study programme, please see:www.science.ku.dk/phd, “Study Structures”.

  Until the MSc degree is obtained, (when exactly two years of the full 3+5 programme remains), the grant will be paid partly in the form of 48 state education grant portions (in Danish: “SU-klip”) plus salary for work (teaching, supervision etc.) totalling a workload of 150 working hours per year. A PhD grant portion is currently (2026) DKK 7,426 before tax.
 
 When you have obtained the MSc degree, you will transfer to the salary-earning part of the scholarship for a period of two years. At that point, the terms of employment and payment will be according to the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and The Danish Confederation of Professional Associations on Academics in the State (AC). The position is covered by the Protocol on Job Structure.

  Responsibilities and tasks in both PhD programmes

   	
• Complete and pass the MSc education in accordance with the curriculum of the MSc programme (ONLY when you are attending the integrated MSc and PhD programme) 	
• Carry through an independent research project under supervision 	
• Complete PhD courses corresponding to approx. 30 ECTS / ½ FTE 	
• Participate in active research environments, including a stay at another research institution, preferably abroad 	
• Teaching and knowledge dissemination activities 	
• Write scientific papers aimed at high-impact journals 	
• Write and defend a PhD thesis on the basis of your project    Application and Assessment Procedure
 Your application including all attachments must be in English and submitted electronically by clicking APPLY FOR POSITION below.

  Please include: 

   	
• Motivated letter of application (max. one page) 	
• Research Statement (max. one page excl. references) detailing your desired research focus. The research statement should demonstrate your independent thinking by outlining a concrete research project within the topic of designing self-tracking technologies for chronic conditions you would wish to explore. This should include specific research questions you aim to address, preliminary ideas on methodological approaches you would employ, connections to existing literature and, if relevant, your previous research, and the potential impact and applications of this research. As we are interested in your own ideas and writing style, please do not use generative AI. 	
• Curriculum vitae including information about your education, experience, language skills and other skills relevant for the position 	
• Original diplomas for Bachelor or Master and transcript of records in the original language, including an authorized English translation if issued in another language than English or Danish. If not completed, a certified/signed copy of a recent transcript of records or a written statement from the institution or supervisor is accepted. 	
• Publication list (if relevant) 	
• Contact information for up to two people who have agreed to provide a reference.   Application deadline: 
 The deadline for applications is 29 November 2026, 23:59 GMT +1.

  We reserve the right not to consider material received after the deadline, and not to consider applications that do not live up to the abovementioned requirements.

  The further process 
 After deadline, a number of applicants will be selected for academic assessment by an unbiased expert assessor. You are notified whether you will be passed for assessment.

  The assessor will assess the qualifications and experience of the shortlisted applicants with respect to the above-mentioned research area, techniques, skills and other requirements. The assessor will conclude whether each applicant is qualified and, if so, for which of the two models. The assessed applicants will have the opportunity to comment on their assessment. You can read about the recruitment process at http://employment.ku.dk/faculty/recruitment-process/.

  Questions
 For specific information about the PhD fellowship, please contact Assistant Professor Sarah Homewood, sfh@di.ku.dk, 31606109.

  General information about PhD study at the Faculty of SCIENCE is available at the PhD School’s website: https://www.science.ku.dk/phd/.

   

  The University of Copenhagen wishes to reflect the surrounding community and invites all regardless of personal background to apply for the position.

Ascendis Pharma is a global biopharmaceutical company committed to making a meaningful difference in patients' lives. Guided by our core values of Patients, Science, and Passion, we are applying our innovative TransCon® technology platform to fulfill our mission of developing new therapies that demonstrate best-in-class potential to address unmet medical needs.

At our headquarters in Hellerup, Denmark, research facilities in Heidelberg, Germany, and additional offices across Europe and the United States, we are advancing programs within our Endocrinology Rare Disease portfolio. We also collaborate with partners on the development of TransCon-based products in other therapeutic areas and markets.

We are seeking a passionate in vivo pharmacologist to join our growing team. jobs.occupation: DIAS Professor in Clinical Translational Psychiatry and Centre Leader for the Elite Centre for Clinical and Translational Psychiatry at Odense University Hospital and the University of Southern Denmark
jobs.description:
The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS), the Department of Clinical Research at the University of Southern Denmark (SDU), and the Region of Southern Denmark seek an outstanding candidate to fill a fully tenured Professor position in the field of clinical translational psychiatry. The candidate is expected to start by agreement.

The candidate is expected to start by agreement.

We seek an exceptional researcher with demonstrated excellence in their discipline and a proven ability to push boundaries, challenge conventions, and engage in groundbreaking interdisciplinary research. The successful candidate will be expected to contribute to cutting-edge advancements in their field while fostering collaboration across disciplines, embracing DIAS’s mission of curiosity-driven research. The ideal candidate will have a strong international research profile, an outstanding record of attracting competitive research funding, and a demonstrated ability to conduct interdisciplinary research. The successful candidate will be attached to the Department of Clinical Research, DIAS, and the Region, and must be prepared to engage in multiple and diverse research environments at SDU and in the Region of Southern Denmark. 

What we offer

• 
The opportunity to lead a new elite centre for clinical and translational psychiatry, with five-year funding of DKK 17 million (equivalent to Euro 2.3 million), with the potential for a five-year extension.

• 
A strong interdisciplinary research environment through DIAS, comprising leading academics across medicine, science, and the humanities, with the opportunity to collaborate with outstanding researchers across SDU’s five faculties.

• 
Access to state-of-the-art research facilities at the newly built Odense University Hospital (OUH), where psychiatry and somatic care are integrated to foster collaboration between these fields.

• 
Comprehensive research support services from DIAS and SDU, targeting prestigious funding such as DNRF, ERC, and grants from Danish private foundations.

• 
If recruited from abroad or from industry, the candidate will be eligible for a fast-track DKK 11 million  (equivalent to Euro 1.5 million ) Lundbeck Foundation Start-Up grant.

• 
Reduced teaching obligations compared to a standard professorship, allowing the candidate to focus on research and leadership within the elite centre.

Who we are looking for 

We are seeking a highly accomplished researcher with expertise in the field of clinical translational psychiatry, who is eager to engage in collaborative activities within the DIAS framework. 

The ideal candidate should demonstrate:

• 
A commitment to engaging in boundary-crossing interdisciplinary research and dialogue. 

• 
A record of internationally competitive research activities at the highest level of ambition. 

• 
Publications in high-level peer-reviewed academic journals and leading innovative research programmes in clinical psychiatry. 

• 
An ability to attract significant external funding to support independent and collaborative research initiatives.

• 
Engagement in the international academic society. 

• 
Extensive experience in building and leading multidisciplinary research teams that integrate basic and clinical sciences, with an emphasis on translational research spanning from laboratory findings to clinical trials.

• 
A research focus in areas such as child and adolescent psychiatry, clinical psychopharmacology, epidemiology, molecular neurobiology, substance use disorders, or serious mental illness.

• 
The ability to develop a translational research programme in one or more of the mentioned fields, with a focus on building cooperative, multidisciplinary teams that bridge basic science and the design and execution of early-phase clinical trials.

• 
A demonstrated commitment to mentorship, teaching, and leadership, fostering the next generation of researchers in interdisciplinary research environments.

• 
Experience at Full or Associate Professor level within relevant fields.

• 
Fluency in English

The Danish Institute for Advanced Study (DIAS)

DIAS at SDU is a hub for interdisciplinary excellence at and beyond the frontier of knowledge, bringing together outstanding researchers from various disciplines to foster groundbreaking interdisciplinary research and bold innovation. DIAS nurtures a collaborative and curiosity-driven environment, encouraging scholars to think outside the box and challenge conventional boundaries. The institute values open-minded exploration and an ambitious yet collegial atmosphere with a strong sense of community. Researchers affiliated with DIAS are expected to contribute actively to DIAS activities, mentor DIAS fellows, and engage in interdisciplinary collaborations across faculties and departments, both nationally and internationally.  

The Department of Clinical Research

The Department of Clinical Research does translational research spanning from basic research to patient care, within both somatics and psychiatry. The interdisciplinary research aims to improve patient treatment, health, and well-being. Researchers at the institute often have joint appointments between clinic, research, and education, ensuring a strong academic foundation for the research at Odense University Hospital (OUH) and in psychiatry. The researchers at the Department of Clinical Research primarily consist of doctors, nurses, and other healthcare professionals with main employment at OUH.

The Centre for Clinical and Translational Psychiatry

The centre will be based at the new Odense University Hospital, which integrates psychiatric and somatic care to promote close collaboration between the fields. The hospital includes a state-of-the-art adult psychiatric department with around 600 employees, 142 single rooms, and specialized sections for joint somatic-psychiatric care, rehabilitation, telepsychiatry, and more. The child and adolescent psychiatric department cover the entire region with about 600 employees, two inpatient wards with a total of 34 beds, and outpatient clinics at four geographical sites.

The centre’s aim is to advance novel psychiatric research through innovative approaches that will significantly impact future patient care. This includes translating discoveries from the laboratory to clinical settings, whether within narrow clinical fields or through broader cross-disciplinary collaborations that involve various clinical functions, professions, and institutions.

Additional information

For further information about being a professor at DIAS, please contact DIAS director Sten Rynning at +45 6550 2193 or via email at director-dias@sdu.dk 

For further information and questions about the position, please contact the Head of the Department of Clinical Research Rikke Leth-Larsen at +456550 3477 or via email at rllarsen@health.sdu.dk or Medical Director Bjarne Dahler-Eriksen, Odense University Hospital, at +4523284068 or via email at bde@rsyd.dk. You may also contact the Vice Dean for Research and Innovation at the Faculty of Health Sciences, SDU, Uffe Holmskov at +45 6550 3775 or via email at uholmskov@health.sdu.dk regarding the position.

Application, salary, and employment terms

This position will be attached to the Department of Clinical Research in Odense. The successful candidate will be expected to regularly engage in DIAS activities and interdisciplinary cooperation in Odense. 

The successful applicant will be employed in accordance with the agreement between the Ministry of Finance and the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). 

For more details on salary and taxation, please refer to the provided links about salary and taxation.

Teaching obligations will be reduced compared to a standard professorship at SDU, allowing more time for research and leadership activities.

Application requirements

Applications must be submitted electronically via the "Apply now" link provided below.

If you experience technical problems, please contact hcm-support@sdu.dk. 

The application must include the following:

• 
A motivation letter.

• 
A detailed Curriculum Vitae (CV), including contacts for possible references.

• 
Copies of relevant certificates/diplomas.

• 
A teaching portfolio detailing previous teaching experience.

• 
A complete list of publications, highlighting those most relevant to the position.

• 
Up to ten of the most relevant publications

• 
A research and publication plan for the next five years, including a description of synergy with the department's activities and the potential to benefit from DIAS’s interdisciplinary environment.

All application materials must be submitted in English, and only applications written in English will be considered.

Submission guidelines

• 
Files must be submitted in PDF format, with each file no larger than 10 MB.

• 
If multiple files are needed for a single section, combine them into one PDF file.

• 
Zip files, image files (jpg, png, etc.), and password-protected PDF files will not be accepted. All PDF files must be unlocked to allow binding.

• 
The application deadline is February 7, 2027, at 23:59 CET. Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

Applications that are incomplete with regards to the above-mentioned requirements will not be assessed by the committee. Shortlisting and tests may be used in the recruitment process and references may be obtained.  

We recommend that international applicants take the time to visit the websites of Work in Denmark and the International Staff Office at SDU. Here you will find information and facts about moving to, working, and living in Denmark.

Assessment

Shortlisting may be used as part of the recruitment process. Read about shortlisting at SDU. 

Assessment of shortlisted applications will be done under the existing Appointment Order for universities. Shortlisted applications will be assessed by an assessment committee. The committee may request additional information, and, if so, it is the responsibility of the applicant to provide the necessary material.  

When the assessment committee has submitted its report, the applicants will receive the part of the evaluation that concerns themselves.

About SDU

SDU is committed to fostering a diverse staff that reflects society’s diversity. We welcome applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of personal background.

SDU was founded in 1966 and now has over 27,000 students, nearly 20% of whom are international. SDU employs more than 3,800 staff and offers 115 study programmes across disciplines such as the humanities, social sciences, natural sciences, health sciences, and engineering. While SDU’s main campus is in Odense, it also has campuses in other locations.

Equal opportunity employment

The University of Southern Denmark is an equal opportunity employer. We consider all qualified applicants without regard to race, colour, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, religion, national origin, age, disability, pregnancy, or any other protected status.

The University of Southern Denmark wishes our staff to reflect the surrounding community and therefore encourages everyone, regardless of personal background, to apply for the position. 

SDU conducts research in critical technologies, which, due to the risk of unwanted knowledge transfer, are subject to several security measures. Therefore, based on information from open sources, background checks may be conducted on candidates for the position.
